texts: good. the dated state is reified so 'Day 21', 'Year 1' and the past tense have something to attach to, and the plain 'the moon was full' form is emitted alongside it, so both 'when was the moon full?' and 'was the moon full?' resolve.

good. the Council and the Watch are both kept as ordinary definite referents with no invented naming, the convening is one event with the Council as its agent, and 'at the Watch' lands as the place it happened.

mixed: the redistributing, the Council as its agent, and 'across the lantern-stations' are all recorded correctly, but bare 'mire-essence' came out as the substance-in-general rather than as the particular store being moved — a kind word sitting where a specific thing should be, so nothing ties the essence here to the essence in your next two sentences. Adding a determiner individuates it: "The Council redistributed the mire-essence across the lantern-stations."

mixed: the Northcove stations, the contributing, and the central pool as destination are all correct (the 'Northcove stations' link in particular came out exactly right), but bare 'mire-essence' again lands as the kind word rather than as a portion taking part in this one occurrence. Same one-word fix: "The Northcove stations contributed some mire-essence to the central pool."

bad: 'the stations of the Middle Row' was read as the stations being physically inside the Middle Row, a containment your sentence never states; the of-phrase should have linked them to the Row the way the parallel 'Northcove stations' was linked to Northcove in the previous sentence. Use that premodifier form, and individuate the essence as above: "The Council issued some mire-essence from the central pool to the Middle Row stations."

bad: 'in the Watch ledgers' was recorded as the place the recording happened — as though the Council had been standing inside the ledgers — instead of as the medium the redistribution was written into. Naming the written record separately removes the ambiguity: "The Council recorded the redistribution, and the entry sits in the Watch ledgers." Your original wording is defensible, so this is as much a translator slip as a phrasing problem, but the two-clause form cannot be misread.
